comments.body:
SESSION "orphans" — 2026-08-09. Triage of every PARENTLESS story/task in open or in_progress (30 tickets), then close/land/decide.

## Method
Listed type=story,task status=open,in_progress and filtered to tickets with no parent. Assessed each against origin/main with five parallel subagents, evidence-based: a plan in a ticket is not progress in the code. Result: 4 effectively complete, 1 fully coded but unpushed, 4 partial, 21 not started.

## Closed (12)
- 556a — landed earlier as a3148ad85b; the operator's temporary closure hold was lifted this session. All 5 ACs verified against the merged file (20 tests pass, single test file touched).
- ae1b — read-only quality audit; deliverable was the two report comments. Closed with --force because it records file_impact (files INSPECTED, not modified) so no commit can reference it. Its own report states "No production or test files were modified."
- 9f7f — SUPERSEDED into bug b636, which landed as 5e7d6e71ba. Residual gap filed as 08c8.
- 696a — proposals LEDGER; every approved item verified landed under its own downstream ticket (7e77, a114, d52a, 4ee2, T1 web, cancellation, provenance lint). Closed --force: no code was ever written under this id.
- 9416 — the unlanded change; see below.
- 2380, 8120, cc99, 81d5 — the four cheap wins, each landed through both Gerrit gates.
- 475e, f391 — analysis tickets, closed with recorded findings.
- 12b7 — closed WON'T FIX; see below.

## Landed (5 Gerrit changes, all merged)
1571 (9416), 1572 (2380), 1573 (8120), 1574 (cc99), 1575 (81d5).

9416's work had been sitting unpushed in a worktree 379 commits behind origin/main. Cherry-picked the single commit onto a fresh worktree instead of rebasing the stack; one conflict in the generated, drift-gated docs/env-vars.md, resolved by taking HEAD and regenerating.

## The most important finding: f391
Replayed the persisted *-REVIEW_RESULT.json sidecars at zero LLM cost (662 plan-v3 reviews / 10,250 verified findings). The `undecomposed` axis fires ~0.1% and its fires are genuine, but:
- The accepted explanation for its rarity is FALSE. G5 suppression is 0.00% — coverage.g5_undecomposed_vetoed is absent from all 2,000 sidecars, and the veto only applies to tickets with children (~9% of reviewed tickets). Code and prompts still assert this suppression happens.
- Its 0.85 impact floor is GRADE-INDEPENDENT: a `low` finding scores like a `high`. In 25 of 29 fires it was the only hard override; one ticket blocked at 0.6072 against a 0.60 line when its impact without the floor was 0.0.
Verdict RETUNE (not keep, not retire). Filed as d4c2.

## Decisions taken on the partials
1. 514d re-scoped to the CODE-REVIEW half only — the plan-review half already landed under d52a.
2+3. 4f40 re-scoped: assess the HISTORICAL impact of lowering the block threshold (counter-factual replay + false-positive audit of every finding a candidate threshold would newly block) before choosing a posture. Current evidence shows max impact 0.5 vs a 0.90 threshold, so flipping the flag at 0.90 would change nothing. criteria_routing.json must not change in that ticket.
4-6. 259c rewritten — see the inventory correction below.
7-10. 06e0 and 5e53 reparented under audit epic 2fe0 (already scoped to LOC/complexity/typing).

## Inventory correction on 259c (I got this wrong twice; recording so the next reader does not)
Most of what 259c originally proposed ALREADY EXISTS:
- p4_oversize (det_floor.py:371) already fires on ALL tickets, is already advisory, and already has THREE dimensions including P4_DESC_SOFT_CAP_CHARS = 24_000. The description-length dimension does not need adding.
- Its three signals accumulate into ONE DetResult, so the duplicate-reporting we wanted to prevent is already impossible. No suppression machinery is needed — that work was cut.
- p6_ac_quality (det_floor.py:470) ALREADY detects compound-AND criteria and already coaches "split so each is independently verifiable". My first inventory reported this as absent; that was wrong — the grep that would have found it was truncated by head -20. Corrected before the ticket was finalized.
- p11_ac_vagueness (det_clarity.py:182) is a BLOCKING per-AC-line vague-lexicon check; p6 runs the same lexicon advisory over the whole plan.
The genuine gaps are only: (a) the AC soft cap of 25 was never derived from data and would not have fired on the 14-AC ticket that motivated the work, and (b) NOTHING detects a VACUOUS criterion — one whose truth a gate already proves ("tests pass", "children complete", "CI green"). Vacuous items must be excluded when calibrating the cap, or the cap is derived from padded counts. Vacuity detection extends p6 (DET, advisory, zero LLM cost) rather than adding a routed LLM criterion.

## 12b7 closed WON'T FIX
Its premise is disproven: the sequential per-criterion recovery loop it targets (completion_recovery.py:583) no longer exists. Worse, the design it proposes — per-criterion fan-out — was already built, measured, and deliberately REMOVED for "exploding token/wall-clock cost", the same grounds the ticket argues from. The surviving concern (the monolithic PRIMARY completion call as wall-clock critical path) is real and should be re-filed against the current batched architecture rather than carried on a plan describing an architecture that no longer exists.

## New tickets filed (5)
08c8 (fsck _repair_ticket bypasses rebuild_with_restore), 50b1 (macOS py3.13 index-lock CI flake), d4c2 (retune the undecomposed axis), ea2a (bound the enrichment queue read), plus the 12b7 follow-up left unfiled by decision.

## Operational findings worth keeping
- MODULE-SIZE CAP IS NOW BINDING. 9416 failed CI's module-size gate because _config_schema.py was EXACTLY at the 800-LOC cap on main; a 9-line comment addition pushed it over. Landed by compressing prose back to exactly 800. This is direct evidence for 5e53, which has regressed: 46 files over 700 LOC (was 40), two at 800/800.
- TESTS MUST RUN FROM A VENV BUILT AGAINST THE TREE UNDER TEST. Running 9416's new tests against a checkout whose editable install pointed at pre-rename source produced 18 spurious failures. Environment artifact, not repository evidence.
- review-plan defaults to --ref origin/main, so from a checkout BEHIND origin/main every attestation reads as stale. Use --ref HEAD.
- The tickets tracker had a stranded index conflict (DU on two SOURCE paths that do not belong on the tickets branch) which blocked ALL ticket writes. Cause: stray untracked working copies of the already-landed measurement-provenance work sitting in .tickets-tracker/, which rebar's sync stashes and pops. Resolved non-destructively: unstaged the paths and MOVED the stray files to /Users/joeoakhart/tracker-stray-files-2026-08-09 rather than deleting them. origin/tickets itself is clean. If ticket writes start failing with "unmerged path(s) in the tracker index", this is the cause.
- The macOS py3.13 leg failed the SAME store index-lock test on two unrelated changes within an hour, forcing a recheck cycle each time. Filed as 50b1 — the risk is training authors to treat red CI as noise.
- 2380's agent DISPROVED its own ticket's premise: the citations' referent is not epic 3006 (created a month after the citations landed) but the pre-extraction DSO epic 3a03-b3f2-b34c-4e4f. Fixing as specified would have swapped one wrong reference for another.

## Left open deliberately
514d, 4f40, 259c (re-scoped, awaiting execution); 06e0, 5e53 (reparented under 2fe0); 732b (waiting on an mcp 2.0.x patch release); 5623 (no ACs and no file_impact, so not claimable as written).

## Housekeeping
Six worktrees remain on disk: closeout-wt, land-9416, task-2380-citations, task-8120-path-cleanup, task-cc99-typecheck-scripts, task-81d5-derive-sweep.
